provenance.paper_title: You Only Demonstrate Once: Category-Level Manipulation from Single Visual Demonstration

latest_version.version_label: arXiv v2 / RSS 2022 paper reviewed on 2026-08-31

representation_paths.memory_component: fixed category-level 6-DoF demonstration trajectory and task-relevant local-frame sequence

evidence.section: Full paper: Sec. IV-B Model-free 6 DoF Object Motion Tracking; Sec. IV-C Category-Level Behavior Cloning
evidence.paraphrase: A single recorded demonstration video is parsed into an ordered object-pose trajectory in the receptacle coordinate frame, lifted into a category-level representation, and reprojected for a novel object. During online execution, Algorithm 1 iterates through the resulting fixed virtual target trajectory and uses each stored pose as the next manipulation goal.

evidence.section: Full paper: Sec. IV-C Local Attention
evidence.paraphrase: A demonstration-derived attention heatmap and local anchor sequence preserve task-relevant geometry along the manipulation horizon; online execution transfers these fixed references to the novel object while the controller follows the stored trajectory.

adjudication_notes: Included under the guide's fixed demonstration-memory rule: the demonstration-derived 6-DoF trajectory persists beyond video parsing and is repeatedly read during later robot execution.

The online object tracker updates the robot's current pose estimate, but the operative demonstration trajectory and its access policy remain fixed. This feedback control is not a persistent memory edit, so the architecture remains T1.
